\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\footnotesize\raggedright
$c^*$: the energy-optimal amplitude of a load case's prediction, from the energy alone (no reference solution); the median over a set's load cases, then seed mean $\pm$ sample SD. $c^*$ is the solution's energy norm over the prediction's, times the cosine between the two in the energy inner product: where the cosine is near 1, $c^*$ above 1 means the prediction's level is too small and below 1 too large, while a small $c^*$ can also mean a poor shape. After $c^*$: the relative energy gap and the displacement error once each load case's prediction is scaled by its $c^*$, which removes the level and leaves the shape (the energy gap after $c^*$ is one minus the squared cosine).\par
Exploratory (PREREG\_W9 Sec. 7): each change is S against the fresh baseline with the Sec. 6 guard computed (lower / worse beyond max(10\%, 2 SE$_\mathrm{rel}$)); no verdict.
\end{minipage}
